case_payload.title: High level with valve feedback inconsistent with operator action

condition_payload.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator failed to open the liquid outlet and caused the high level. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

surface_form_payload.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

candidate_causes.cause_description: LV-101 failed to open and remained closed despite open command, blocking liquid outflow from V-001 and causing More liquid deviation.

evidence_against.relevance: Command-feedback mismatch alone does not prove mechanical sticking; actuator, signal-path, or feedback instrumentation fault could produce same observation without inspection.
Withheld reference cause list prevents excluding other HAZOP causes for high level.

evidence_for.relevance: Open command issued but position feedback remained closed, indicating outlet remained blocked during level rise.
Blocked liquid outflow directly produces the defined deviation of More liquid in V-001.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Operator failed to open the liquid outlet or to intervene manually via LV-101/LV-102 during the level increase.

evidence_against.relevance: LV-101 did receive an open command yet remained closed, contradicting failure-to-command as decisive blockage.
Alarms generated records but packet provides no response timeline, procedure, or HMI data to establish failure to act.
No procedures or defined expected use of LV-102 provided to define required operator action.

evidence_for.relevance: No manual command to LV-101 or LV-102 was recorded during level increase, consistent with absence of manual intervention.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Electrical or instrumentation fault in LV-101 actuation, signal path, or position feedback preventing opening or misreporting position.

evidence_against.relevance: Sustained More liquid deviation suggests outlet was truly closed, making pure feedback misreport without actual closure less likely though not excluded.
No loop checks, maintenance data, or actuator diagnostics provided to confirm instrumentation fault.

evidence_for.relevance: Discrepancy between commanded open and feedback closed is also the signature of actuator/signal failure or feedback error.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Other unknown process or safeguard-related cause not resolvable from packet.

evidence_against.relevance: Confirmed LV-101 commanded open but remaining closed provides sufficient proximate explanation for accumulation.
High and high-high alarms generated records, indicating level detection was at least partly functional.

evidence_for.relevance: Reference cause list withheld, so unassessed HAZOP causes remain possible.
Safeguard closing action of SDV-30010 is defined but its actual response during event is not evidenced.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: More liquid in V-001 requires outflow blocked relative to inflow. E1 provides direct mechanism: LV-101 was commanded open but remained closed. This contradicts the hypothesis that no open command was given and makes valve failure the most defensible proximate cause. E2 shows no manual command, but without procedures and LV-102 role definition it cannot establish operator omission as causal, especially since LV-101 would not have opened. E3 confirms LAH-102/LAHH-103 alarmed, leaving mechanical sticking versus actuation/instrumentation fault unresolved.
uncertainty_notes: Source-derived possible-cause list withheld per CASE-05; completeness of alternatives cannot be verified.
LV-101/LV-102 service and source of LV-101 open command (automatic vs manual) not explicitly defined; outlet function inferred from context.
No valve inspection, maintenance, or actuator diagnostics to distinguish mechanical sticking from electrical/instrumentation failure.
Actual response of SDV-30010 to LAH-102/LAHH-103 and V-001 inflow conditions not evidenced.
No operator procedures, alarm response expectations, or HMI visibility data to judge required manual intervention.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-HIGHLEVEL-01__operator_hypothesis__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Level — More liquid in separator vessel V-001.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Flooding of vessel V-001.; Liquid carryover into the gas line and treatment unit.; Possible damage to the unit generators.; Unit shutdown.; Loss of production.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: LAHH-103 with closing action of SDV-30010.; LAH-102 with closing action of SDV-30010.
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] LV-101 received an open command, but valve-position feedback remained closed.
[E2] No manual command to LV-101 or LV-102 was recorded during the level increase.
[E3] LAH-102 and LAHH-103 were present and generated alarm records.

# Proposed causal hypothesis
The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator failed to open the liquid outlet and caused the high level. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

# Task
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.
Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. The proposed hypothesis is not established fact.
